- Family and target: h1 (notes/hooks.md), sketch i01. Medium target, Hard welcome (user, 2026-10-12: "there is no
  slot for Easy Tier for this bundle, we should target medium and high"). Measured platform result pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 8 para 81 with footnote 14 (L307, L316): three MNOs "collectively have 75% of the fixed
  broadband market", from the Commission's "Annual Telecommunications Monitoring Report: Key Facts, 20 December
  2017". Doc 8 para 48 (L211): 2degrees "well behind Spark (incl Skinny) and Vodafone in total subscriber shares",
  so the two largest are Spark and Vodafone. Doc 7 footnote 7 (L320), repeated in footnote 23 (L601): 2degrees 4%
  "by connections", from the "2017 Annual Telecommunications Monitoring Report, 20 December 2017". 75 - 4 = 71.
- Universe: not applicable (single value).
- Necessity: Doc 8 is the only source of a mobile-operator total for fixed broadband (L307-308). Doc 7 is the only
  source of 2degrees' fixed broadband share (L320, L601). Searched all eleven texts for "broadband market",
  "market share", "retail broadband", "broadband retailer", "75%", "80%", "71%", "4%" and "13%": the only other
  hit is Doc 2 L38. Without Doc 7 the third operator cannot be taken out of 75%; without Doc 8 there is no total
  to take it from. Doc 2 is left unticked: it carries only the figure the answer rejects, and removing it removes
  that figure. No removal probe run.
- Selected-lever checks: right edition: Doc 2 is dated "30 November 2017" (L6) and its Commission citations are to
  the "2016 Annual Telecommunications Monitoring Report, May 2017" (footnote 2, L31); the 80% sentence (L38) has no
  footnote. Scatter: 75 and 4 sit in different submissions. Wrong routes: 75 (total for part), 80 (Chorus). Both
  differ from 71.
- Targeted failure modes: mode 1 (Part vs total, takes the wrong line item) -> 75%: Doc 8 L307 prints the
  three-operator total and no two-operator figure. Mode 2 (Wrong year or edition, uses the wrong period or date)
  -> 80%: Doc 2 L38 is the only sentence in the bundle about "the two largest mobile network owners" and
  broadband, and it predates the December 2017 report. Neither is measured yet. Considered and not declared:
  Linking across documents (true of the join, but it names no wrong answer of its own).
- Calculation verification: Python, 2026-10-12: 75 - 4 = 71. Whole percentages as printed; no rounding step.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no document prints 71%. The page overview does not mention fixed broadband shares
  for Doc 7 or Doc 2; for Doc 8 it lists "75% MNO fixed broadband market share" among its figures, which names
  the total and not the two-operator share. Shortest route: Doc 8's total, the identity of the third operator,
  Doc 7's footnote, one subtraction.
- Precision/readings: both inputs are whole percentages from one report, so the difference is a whole percentage.
  "Fixed broadband market" follows Doc 8's wording; Doc 7's "by connections" is the same report's basis. "Two
  largest mobile network operators" cannot mean a pair that includes 2degrees (Doc 8 L211; Doc 7 footnote 9,
  L347, treats 2degrees as outside "the two largest MNO").
- Completeness: full corpus, no gaps (notes/intake.json; notes/doc-map.md).
- Style/set review: 25 words. q02 uses different documents' facts (plan prices) and a different mechanism; no

- Warnings answered: see the hand-over note; filled after the floor run.

sections.question: On the Commerce Commission's December 2017 monitoring figures, what share of the fixed broadband market, to the nearest percent, did New Zealand's two largest mobile network operators hold together?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 8, product bundling section): Covec reads the Commerce Commission's most recent monitoring report, its Key Facts edition of December 2017, as showing that the three mobile network operators collectively have 75 per cent of the fixed broadband market.

Step 2. Source input (Doc 8, roaming regulation section): the three operators are Spark, Vodafone and 2degrees, and 2degrees is well behind Spark and Vodafone in subscriber shares. The two largest operators are therefore Spark and Vodafone, and the collective figure also holds the share of the third operator, 2degrees.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 7, footnote to its answer on bundling): on the Commission's annual monitoring report of the same December date, 2degrees' own share of broadband connections was 4 per cent.

Step 4. Calculation (Doc 8 and Doc 7): the two largest operators' share is the three-operator figure less the third operator's share: 75 − 4 = 71. Spark and Vodafone together held that percentage of the fixed broadband market.

Step 5. Check on the printed look-alike (Doc 2): Chorus says the two largest mobile network owners account for 80 per cent of the retail broadband market. Chorus wrote on 30 November 2017, before the December report existed, and gives no source for the figure, so it is not the Commission's December figure and is not used.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Part vs total
How a careless solver fails: Takes the wrong line item

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Wrong year or edition
How a careless solver fails: Uses the wrong period or date

Why these are traps: Part vs total: Doc 8's 75% is all three operators' fixed broadband share; taking it for the two largest gives 75%. Wrong edition: Doc 2's 80%, written 30 November 2017, predates the December report. The gold removes 2degrees' 4% (Doc 7) from 75%: 71%.
